title: Real elevators run on algorithms with names. I rebuilt them faithfully, it made my game no more fun, so I took the controls myself
author: office-canard
selftext:
LOOK EV started with someone else's problem. Food delivery drivers get stuck in the elevators of tall apartment buildings, sometimes spending thirty minutes on one drop just riding up and down. So the first version put you in the driver's shoes: deliver the orders by using the elevators and stairs as efficiently as you can.



To make the elevators believable, I looked up how real ones work. They run on named algorithms: the LOOK method, and group control for managing a whole bank of cars. That's where the title comes from. So I built them faithfully.



It changed nothing. However realistic the elevators got, the delivery game wasn't any more fun.



So I switched sides. What if you control the elevators and step into the group control system? But there was no room to step in. Of course there wasn't. Professionals designed that system to be optimal. The realism was so complete that it left the player nothing to do.



So I thought, forget stepping in. I'll just drive the thing myself. The moment I did, it looked like Mini Metro, and the whole game came together at once.



How it plays:



\- You run the elevator by hand. Pick up the people waiting on each floor and take them where they want to go.

\- Every stage is one day, 24 hours squeezed into a minute or two. In the morning, people come down from every floor to the lobby. In the evening, they head back up.

\- As the buildings get taller, you can't keep up alone. That's when the LOOK and group control elevators I built at the start come back, as your coworkers. First one automatic car runs beside you, later two.

\- And one kind of passenger moves between floors with no pattern at all: the delivery driver. The person the whole game started with came back as the one you can't predict.



How AI fit in: Claude wrote the code, including the LOOK and group control elevators. The music is Claude too. I told it to synthesize city pop, and I'm really happy with how it came out. The people are icon assets.
